ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two pie charts in the image. The left side is labeled Human (70 kilograms), and below it is written Total oxygen store: 1.95 liters. The right side is labeled Weddell seal (450 kilograms), and below it is written Total oxygen store: 25.9 liters. Reasoning: The oxygen storage per kilogram of body weight for humans is 1.95 ÷ 70 ≈ 0.028 L/kg. The oxygen storage per kilogram of body weight for Weddell seal is 25.9 ÷ 450 ≈ 0.058 L/kg. Comparing the two, 0.058 ÷ 0.028 ≈ 2.1, about 2 times. Therefore, the oxygen stored per kilogram of body weight by Weddell seal is approximately twice that of humans.
